items.title: Durkheim's 1897 finding
items.claim: In Le Suicide (1897), Emile Durkheim argued that suicide rates depend on social, not individual, factors. Which pattern did he report?

options.text: Catholics had higher rates than Protestants
Protestants had higher rates than Catholics, and the unmarried higher than the married
No religious or marital differences existed
Rates were identical across all European countries

items.reveal_title: Group integration mattered more than personal pathology
items.reveal:
Durkheim correlated rates with degree of social integration. Higher integration (Catholic, married, wartime) tended to predict lower rates.

Later critics (Douglas, 1967) questioned the reliability of historical suicide records.
items.why: Durkheim's argument founded sociology as a discipline studying 'social facts' independent of individual minds.

items.title: What Marx predicted
items.claim: Karl Marx predicted that capitalism would generate growing inequality and eventual crisis. Recent empirical work (Piketty, 2014) examined wealth concentration over centuries. What was a headline finding?

options.text: Wealth inequality has steadily fallen since 1800
When the rate of return on capital exceeds growth, wealth concentrates
Inequality is impossible to measure historically

items.reveal_title: r greater than g concentrates wealth
items.reveal:
Piketty's Capital in the Twenty-First Century (2014) used tax records across France, UK, US and others to argue that when the return on capital (r) exceeds the economic growth rate (g), inherited wealth grows faster than earned income.

The book's data and conclusions remain contested but reopened debates Marx began.
items.why: Empirical historical economics revived classical sociological questions about class structure.

items.title: Foucault's panopticon
items.claim: Michel Foucault's Discipline and Punish (1975) used what 18th-century architectural design to illustrate modern power?
items.reveal_title: Bentham's never-built prison became a model of modern surveillance
items.reveal:
Bentham proposed the panopticon in 1791 as a circular building where inmates could be observed at any moment without knowing when.

Foucault argued the principle, the internalisation of an unseen watcher, had spread to schools, factories and clinics.
items.why: Power in modernity, Foucault argued, often works through visibility rather than coercion.
